newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua told to pay $20,000 human rights fine.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua told to pay $20,000 human rights fine.

text.p: Nicaragua has been ordered by an international human rights court to pay a $20,000 fine for delays in resolving the 1990 slaying of a teenager near a former army chief's motorcade, the government said on Saturday.
The Inter-American Court of Human Rights in San Jose, Costa Rica, ruled on Friday the Nicaraguan army had obstructed the investigation into the murder of Jean Paul Genie, 16.
Genie was killed by machine-gun fire after his car allegedly passed former Nicaraguan Army chief Humberto Ortega's motorcade on a road outside Managua on Oct. 28, 1990.

In June 1994, a Nicaraguan military tribunal acquitted Ortega's seven-man security team of murder charges, and Ortega himself of covering up the crime, for lack of evidence after a civilian court passed the case to military jurisdiction.

The international court said Nicaragua's justice system had taken too long to resolve the case, which is still under appeal before the country's Supreme Court, and called for its speedy and just resolution,

Nicaragua "accepts the terms of the sentence given by the Inter-American Court of Human Rights and will proceed to fulfil its terms in conformity with Nicaraguan law," a Foreign Ministry statement said after the fine was issued.
President Arnoldo Aleman, who took power on Jan. 10, told reporters on Friday his government would honour its international human rights commitments. Nicaragua would pay the fine to Genie's family.
